fixes.explanation: Nice try, friend, but nobody gets turned back into wood here. “But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.” (Exodus 7:12) Picture a whole row of magicians holding their serpents up proud, and then ONE serpent just goes down the line like it's late for lunch. I think a few of those magicians checked their hands afterward just to be sure they still had a staff.

You got it, baker. “Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.” Pharaoh is Egypt’s king, and he had just seen Aaron’s staff swallow up the other staffs. That's a lot to see and still not listen. I'd have been asking for a replay, and his mind was already made up.

Sons aren't named in this scene, friend. The text says Aaron raised the staff and struck the Nile “in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials…” (Exodus 7:20). Pharaoh is Egypt’s king. So the people the text puts right there are the king’s own officials, front row, no way to say they missed it.

That’s it, baker. “So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.” ALL of them, digging, shovels out, staring at the ground like it owes them something. I think that's what it looks like when nobody has a backup plan.

Rainwater isn't in the text, friend. It says the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river (Exodus 7:24). No jars lined up on the roof, no clouds mentioned. I'd have grabbed a jar and hoped too, but this verse has shovels, not weather.
